manifest.notes: Deterministic rules derived from data/regulations/excerpts.json (real EgyptERA circulars and Egyptian law, paraphrased research summary - see excerpts.json manifest caveat). Condition nodes are a small safe DSL (no eval of stored code): {all:[...]} / {any:[...]} / {not:node} / {field, op, value}. Valid ops: eq, ne, in, not_in, gt, gte, lt, lte, contains. Evaluated against a fixed context: connectionModel, ownershipStatus, recommended_capacity_kw, gis_codes (set of GisFinding.code present). Rules are mutually exclusive within each connection model by design (capacity/ownership bands do not overlap) so at most one capacity-band finding fires per connection model.

rules.title: Site control (ownership/lease/right-of-use) not confirmed
rules.title_template: Site control must be confirmed before connection approval
rules.explanation_template: EgyptERA requires the applicant to demonstrate site control before connection approval: ownership, or a lease/right-of-use agreement covering the installation site for at least 25 years, expressly authorizing installation and operation of the solar plant. This has not been confirmed for this assessment.
rules.authority: Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA)
requiredDocuments: Ownership deed, or lease/right-of-use agreement covering at least 25 years and expressly authorizing the solar installation

rules.title: Self-consumption up to 500 kW: permit/licence-exempt tier
rules.title_template: Self-consumption connection is supported at this capacity
rules.explanation_template: At this capacity (up to 500 kW) a subscriber-owned self-consumption plant may qualify for an exemption from the electricity-generation permit and licence. The plant must not export power to the grid and must be installed by an NREA-qualified company.
rules.authority: Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA)

rules.title: Self-consumption 500 kW-30 MW: permit and grid-impact study required
rules.title_template: Above 500 kW: EgyptERA permit, licence, and grid-impact study required
rules.explanation_template: Above 500 kW, self-consumption projects require an EgyptERA construction permit, an electricity-generation licence, and a grid-impact/network-impact study at the subscriber's cost, plus any network reinforcement identified by the distribution company. Capacity must also not exceed the facility's maximum recorded electrical demand from the preceding financial year.
rules.authority: Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA)

rules.title: Self-consumption capacity exceeds the 30 MW ceiling
rules.title_template: Recommended capacity exceeds the self-consumption ceiling
rules.explanation_template: Self-consumption plant capacity is capped at 30 MW per subscriber. The recommended capacity exceeds this ceiling and cannot proceed as a standard self-consumption interconnection.
rules.authority: Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA)

rules.title: Net-metering capacity within the published scheme ceiling
rules.title_template: Net-metering connection is within the published capacity band
rules.explanation_template: The recommended capacity is within the 20 MW net-metering scheme ceiling, though connection still depends on capacity available on the local distribution network. The published process includes NREA local-content review (~15 days), distribution-company capacity confirmation (~1 week), construction (up to 6 months for plants up to 500 kW, up to 1 year for larger plants), testing (~3 weeks), and energization (~3 weeks). At least 25% local content is required, reviewed through the NREA PV-HUB process.
rules.authority: Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA)

rules.title: Net-metering capacity exceeds the published scheme ceiling
rules.title_template: Recommended capacity exceeds the net-metering scheme ceiling
rules.explanation_template: The published net-metering procedures cover projects up to 20 MW, subject to available distribution-network capacity. The recommended capacity exceeds this scheme ceiling.
rules.authority: Egyptian Electric Utility and Consumer Protection Regulatory Agency (EgyptERA)

rules.title: Site intersects a protected area
rules.title_template: Site intersects a protected area; separate activity permit likely required
rules.explanation_template: The site intersects a declared protected area in the loaded GIS layer. Constructing facilities or undertaking industrial activity inside a protected area requires approval from the competent environmental authority; confirm with the EEAA Nature Conservation Sector whether a separate protected-area activity permit is required.
rules.authority: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), under Protected Areas Law No. 102 of 1983

rules.title: Environmental-impact assessment required for industrial solar
rules.explanation_template: Industrial solar installations require EEAA environmental review before construction or operation; the residential exemption does not apply. Compact solar installations are typically handled as a Category B project (commonly reviewed within about 30 days), though the final classification depends on plant capacity, location, and environmental sensitivity.
